elements.element: Vendor assigns to Customer all right, title and interest in deliverables created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The assignment covers only deliverables created specifically for Client in the course of the Support Services. Nothing establishes that all deliverables created for Client must fall within that additional condition.

elements.element: Vendor assigns to Customer all right, title and interest in work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The assignment similarly limits work product to that created specifically for Client in the course of the Support Services, rather than covering all work product created for Client.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: TrueLink Intellectual Property existing prior to the Support Services is expressly excluded from the assignment to Client.

elements.element: Vendor grants Customer a licence to Vendor intellectual property embedded in the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The embedded-IP licence applies only to TrueLink Intellectual Property embedded in the defined subset of deliverables created specifically for Client during the Support Services; it does not demonstrably cover Vendor IP embedded in any other deliverables created for Client.

elements.element: The embedded Vendor-IP licence is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The licence is expressly stated to be perpetual.

elements.element: The embedded Vendor-IP licence is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The licence is expressly stated to be irrevocable.

elements.element: The embedded Vendor-IP licence is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The licence is expressly stated to be royalty-free.

elements.element: Customer retains all right, title and interest in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Client expressly retains all right, title and interest in all data of Client and its borrowers, loan applicants, customers and brokers, including Credit Data. The preserved Section 8(d) licence does not transfer ownership.

elements.element: The ownership allocation creates no joint ownership.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly disclaims joint ownership of Client assets and data, assigns all right, title and interest in covered deliverables and work product to Client, and separately excludes retained TrueLink IP.

elements.element: Vendor owns generic tools.
elements.evidence: Tools appear in the definition of TrueLink Intellectual Property, but the assignment excludes them only if they existed previously or were developed independently of the Support Services. Generic tools developed during the Support Services are not categorically retained by TrueLink.

elements.element: Vendor owns know-how.
elements.evidence: Know-how appears in the definition of TrueLink Intellectual Property, but there is no categorical Vendor-ownership reservation for know-how; only pre-existing or independently developed TrueLink IP is excluded from assignment.

elements.element: Customer receives rights covering all deliverables.
elements.evidence: Client receives ownership of deliverables created specifically for it during the Support Services, but the language does not demonstrably cover all deliverables under the Agreement.

elements.element: Customer's rights in the deliverables are perpetual.
elements.evidence: The assignment of all right, title and interest has no reversion or time limit, and the licence for embedded TrueLink IP is expressly perpetual.

elements.element: Customer's rights in the deliverables are irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The assignment is unconditional and contains no revocation right, while the embedded-IP licence is expressly irrevocable.

elements.element: Customer's rights in the deliverables are worldwide.
elements.evidence: The assignment has no territorial limitation, and the embedded-IP licence is expressly worldwide.

elements.element: Customer's rights in the deliverables are royalty-free.
elements.evidence: No royalty applies to the assignment, and the embedded-IP licence is expressly royalty-free.

elements.element: Customer may use the deliverables.
elements.evidence: Ownership of the covered deliverables includes the right to use them, and use of embedded TrueLink IP is expressly licensed.

elements.element: Customer may modify the deliverables.
elements.evidence: Ownership of the covered deliverables includes modification rights, and the embedded-IP licence expressly includes the right to modify.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense the deliverables.
elements.evidence: Ownership of the covered deliverables permits licensing them, and the embedded-IP licence expressly includes the right to sublicense.

elements.element: Customer may exercise its deliverable rights for its business.
elements.evidence: The embedded-IP licence expressly permits use, modification and sublicensing for the purposes of Client's business, while Client's ownership rights are broader.

result.reason: Neither level is fully satisfied. The preferred position is incomplete because the assignment and embedded-IP licence are conditioned on creation during the Support Services, without establishing that this captures all deliverables and work product created for Client. The fallback is also incomplete because generic tools and know-how are not categorically reserved to TrueLink and not all deliverables are demonstrably covered. The redline preserves TrueLink's Interface ownership and the existing Credit Data licence, but drafting is weakened by the limited assignment scope, the awkward embedded-IP antecedent, and inherited numbering and definition errors.
